recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-35861 unless a future work group decision changes how serial numbers represented as typed identifiers should be searched.
issue_request: FHIR-35861 was Published as Persuasive with Modification for R5 Device. The approved motion kept the identifier search parameter named identifier with expression Device.identifier, modified the serial-number search parameter to cover both Device.serialNumber and Device.identifier.where(type='SNO'), and kept the Device attributes as-is.
initial_application: The issue was applied by commit 7205ce8c81429aa371fc1517d754a098f6483687, which changed source/device/bundle-Device-search-params.xml so Device-serial-number uses Device.serialNumber | Device.identifier.where(type='SNO'). The current source still contains that expression, and no later Jira-tagged history was found reversing this search-parameter decision.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini has an active [resources] entry device=Device, confirming build scope. Current Device.identifier and Device.serialNumber comments also retain earlier related clarification from FHIR-32559. OO Confluence minutes record the 10-0-1 modified FHIR-35861 motion; the same minutes mention FHIR-35973, but that issue concerns Device.udiCarrier.issuer cardinality and does not alter this identifier/serial-number decision. Focused Zulip searches found no Device-specific community discussion that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The active Device search-parameter bundle already has Device-identifier on Device.identifier and Device-serial-number on Device.serialNumber | Device.identifier.where(type='SNO'), exactly matching the approved FHIR-35861 search behavior.

related_jiras.note: Earlier published Device issue added explanatory Device.serialNumber language that supports keeping Device attributes as-is while FHIR-35861 adjusts search behavior.
Co-minuted Device issue checked during reconciliation; it concerns Device.udiCarrier.issuer cardinality, not serial-number or identifier search semantics.
